title: Work cost of the circuit learner
statement: For natural numbers $n$, $d$, and $s$, and a rational learning parameter $\varepsilon$ satisfying $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$, define the circuit learner's work cost to be the low-degree learner's work cost on $n$ inputs, with degree cutoff given by the circuit learning degree determined by $d$, $s$, and $\varepsilon$.
